questions.key_step: Entries of BA with A symmetric give linear equations.
questions.justification: Linear system for a 2x2 symmetric matrix; one non-linear equation reduces after substitution.

questions.key_step: Peel |Adj M|=|M|^(n-1) and |kM|=k^n|M| layer by layer.
questions.justification: Standard adjoint-determinant identities applied twice, exponent bookkeeping, then solving an exponent equation.

questions.key_step: Count 4-tuples in 0..4 with sums 3,5,7,11 using (1-x^5)^4(1-x)^-4.
questions.justification: Bounded stars and bars over four sums; the cap needs inclusion-exclusion for sums >= 5.

questions.key_step: Compare first row of A^3 with A to get ac=-3/2 and a+3c=-1.
questions.justification: Multiplying a symbolic 3x3 matrix twice, choosing the right entries, then locating a quadratic root; numerical format.

questions.key_step: Choose occupied boxes with every row non-empty, then 5!.
questions.justification: Casework over row occupancy with a figure; one organising idea.

questions.key_step: All triples minus collinear triples (O on both lines).
questions.justification: Standard collinear-triangle count with one trap (O on both lines).

questions.key_step: Forced captain/vice-captain lowers the minimum to 3 and 3.
questions.justification: Short casework once the forced members are accounted for.

questions.key_step: Sets, not arrangements: C(12,2)C(13,2).
questions.justification: One-line product of two combinations.

questions.key_step: Blocks of girls and boys; subtract B1,B2 adjacent.
questions.justification: Standard together/apart count.

questions.key_step: Case by girls from group A: three cases.
questions.justification: Three routine cases of products of combinations.

questions.key_step: Allowed (first,last) pairs times 8^3, minus 50000.
questions.justification: Pair listing with a boundary trap (50000 itself).

questions.key_step: List digit multisets with sum 11 and count arrangements.
questions.justification: Multiset enumeration and arrangements with repeated digits.

questions.key_step: Numerator = (k+1)(k+2)(k+3) - 1 turns each term into 1/k! - 1/(k+3)!.
questions.justification: Needs the factorisation insight, then step-3 telescoping; short once seen.

questions.key_step: Total triples minus collinear triples.
questions.justification: Textbook one-line count.

questions.key_step: Block sizes in dictionary order (24,12,12) then list the O block.
questions.justification: Standard dictionary-rank with repeated letters; slight care over duplicates.

questions.key_step: Unlabelled equal groups then 3! for naming: 9!/(3!)^3.
questions.justification: Distinguishing labelled and unlabelled groups is the usual trap.

questions.key_step: Cases by repeated letters among the 5 chosen.
questions.justification: Three-case selection from a multiset; easy to double-count.

questions.key_step: (mn)!/((m!)^n n!) counts groupings, so integrality needs no computation.
questions.justification: Idea availability: recognising factorial ratios as grouping counts is uncommon.

questions.key_step: Identical books/shelves means partitions of 8 into at most 4 parts.
questions.justification: Short listing of partitions.

questions.key_step: Pascal collapses LHS to 8C(m+2); then 1/n = 1/8.
questions.justification: Two small identities then substitution.
